# GEO report: quay-store **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points). How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. The score is capped at 40 because `robots.txt` blocks Googlebot from the whole site. I assumed you want to be found by search and AI tools, because there is no `geo.config.json`. Nothing is unknown here. The code decides every rule, and the score is low because of four things: the Googlebot block, client-only rendering, a missing `lang`, and an empty description. All of these are results read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot - **Why it matters:** Googlebot is the crawler for Google Search. `Disallow: /` tells it not to read any page, so Google can't index the site. It also lowers the score on GEO-009 and GEO-014. - **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small. Delete the Googlebot group (lines 4–5). The `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` group already allows everyone. - **Score after this:** 72/100. The 40 cap is lifted and 009 and 014 earn their points (18 ÷ 25). ### 2. Send page content in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** Server HTML is what a crawler receives before any JavaScript runs. With `ssr = false`, every page arrives as an empty shell and the text is built only in the browser. Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see nothing. - **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` - **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line, or set `ssr = true` or `prerender = true`. These pages have no browser-only code, so that should be safe. - **Score after this:** 84/100 once item 1 is also done (21 ÷ 25). On its own it still shows 40 because of the cap. ### 3. Add `lang` to the page and write a description for /shop - **Why it matters:** `lang` tells tools which language the page is in. `/shop` has an empty description, so it has no summary to show. - **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` - **What the code says:** `` and `` - **Size:** Small. Use `` and write a real description, for example "Bilge pumps, cleats and rope for boats." - **Score after this:** 92/100 once items 1–3 are done (23 ÷ 25). `/search` also has no description, but it is noindex, so I left it out. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sensible size | Clear | `static/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny file | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Problem | `static/robots.txt:4-5`, site-wide Googlebot block | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | `/` and `/shop` are blocked for Googlebot by `robots.txt:4-5`. `/search` is deliberately noindex and isn't listed or linked, so I excluded it. | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Clear | `/` and `/shop` have absolute canonicals on `https://quay.example`, matching the sitemap and robots. `/search` is noindex and I left it out. | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`, all routes | | GEO-004 | Structured data is valid and complete | Problem | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`. The Product has only `name`. Google's Product docs also expect `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating`. I judged this from my knowledge of those docs, not from a rule file I could check, so treat it as less certain than the others. | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Clear | `static/sitemap.xml`, `Sitemap:` line at `robots.txt:7` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang`. `/shop` has an empty description (`shop/+page.svelte:3`). | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by real links | Clear | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5`, `` links to `/` and `/shop` | | GEO-017 | No page-wide snippet block | Clear | Only `data-nosnippet` on one element (`+layout.svelte:7`), which is a deliberate choice | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | I read the layout and 3 pages. There are no images, links have text, and every page has a title. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not an app project | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | No `llms.txt`. Not scored, and not a problem. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not an app | ## Other problems found - **The sitemap says "index these" while `robots.txt` says "Googlebot, stay out".** Lines 4–5 of `static/robots.txt` contradict `static/sitemap.xml:3-4`, which lists `https://quay.example/` and `https://quay.example/shop`. Removing the Googlebot group (item 1) fixes it. ## Worth considering - **Make /shop list real products:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:9`: `

Bilge pumps, cleats and rope.

`. The page promises "All parts" but only names three categories. Giving each product its own page and address, with a link from the shop, gives readers and crawlers something to find and cite. - **Complete the Product data:** `shop/+page.svelte:5`: `"@type":"Product","name":"Bilge pump"`. This is a single product on a page that is a category list. If you add product pages, put the price, availability and image on each one as `offers`, and drop the Product from the list page. - **Put the delivery terms where they can be read:** `src/routes/+layout.svelte:7`: `
Free delivery over £50.
`. The `data-nosnippet` looks deliberate, so I'd leave it. But the site has no ordinary text anywhere that answers delivery cost, speed or returns. A delivery page, linked from the nav, would answer it. - **Back up "shipped next day":** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7`: `

Marine parts, shipped next day

`. Nothing says the cutoff time, the countries or the carrier. A short line on the home page or a delivery page would support the claim. - **Say who you are and where:** nothing in the code states the business's name, address or contact details. Organization and WebSite structured data using the details you already show would label that for machines. - **Add `viewport` and a `
` element:** `src/app.html:4`: ``, with no `viewport` meta tag. `
%sveltekit.body%
` on line 8 isn't a `
`, which gives tools no clear marker for where the page's main content is. - **Make the home page link onward:** `src/routes/+page.svelte` has only a heading and links to nothing. Link to `/shop` and to key categories in the page body, not only the nav. - **Make titles say who and what:** `shop/+page.svelte:2`: `Shop all parts`. Something like "Boat parts: pumps, cleats, rope | Quay" says more, and it names the brand like the home title does. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `static/sitemap.xml:3` lists URLs with no dates. If you know when pages last changed, add them. A framework-generated sitemap would stay in step with your routes. - **Set the site's URL in one place:** `https://quay.example` is hardcoded in each page and in `robots.txt` and the sitemap. A single base-URL setting in code would avoid mismatches if the domain changes. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Real status codes:** I can't tell from code whether `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and the listed pages answer 200 on the live host. A live scan would confirm this. - **Training crawlers:** `robots.txt` doesn't block `GPTBot` or `ClaudeBot`. That's a separate choice and I haven't counted it. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. - `https://quay.example` is your intended domain. It appears consistently in the canonicals, sitemap and `robots.txt`. - `/search` is deliberately noindex and kept out of the sitemap and nav. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
